September Movie Preview

by Keith Kimbell — September 1, 2026 at 2:37 PM PDT

"Resident Evil (2026)" (Sony/Columbia Pictures/Dušan Martinček)

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 12:14
Instaread

The month ahead will bring Zach Cregger's take on Resident Evil, an Oasis documentary, the return of Shaun the Sheep, and more. To help you plan your moviegoing options, our editors have selected the most notable films releasing in September, listed in alphabetical order.

Atonement

1 / 21

74
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Quinzaine 2026/Jon Peter/Kino Lorber

Drama - dir. Reed Van Dyk
In theaters September 28

For his feature debut, director Reed Van Dyk adapts Dexter Filkins' 2012 New Yorker article, "Atonement After Iraq," about a U.S. Marine (Boyd Holbrook) attempting to reconcile with the woman (Hiam Abbass) whose family he killed. Kenneth Branagh also stars as Michael Reid, a version of Filkins. The film makes its way to U.S. theaters this month after premiering during this year's Cannes Director's Fortnight, where Abbass and Holbrook earned praise for their performances.

Advertisement

Bad Apples

2 / 21

68
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Republic Pictures / Courtesy of TIFF

Comedy/Thriller - dir. Jonatan Etzler
In theaters September 18

The English-language debut from Swedish director Jonatan Etzler (One More Time) stars Saoirse Ronan as Maria, an elementary school teacher at a private school, who takes drastic measures to deal with one of her students, the unruly Danny (Eddie Waller). Adapted by Jess O'Kane from Danish author Rasmus Lindgren's De O önskade, this entertaining dark comedy earned good reviews when it debuted at TIFF last year.

Advertisement

Barbara Forever

3 / 21

91
MetascoreUniversal acclaim
Photo by Strand Releasing

Documentary - dir. Brydie O'Connor
In theaters September 4

Brydie O'Connor's debut feature-length documentary is an archive-driven portrait of pioneering lesbian avant-garde filmmaker Barbara Hammer. Told through Hammer's voice and films, it took home Best Documentary/Essay Film from this year's Berlin International Film Festival and the Jonathan Oppenheim Editing Award at Sundance. Excellent early reviews promise a documentary that's as entertaining as it is informative.

Advertisement

Call My Agent! The Movie

4 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Christophe Brachet/Netflix

Foreign/Comedy/Drama - dir. Émilie Noblet
Streams on Netflix beginning September 10

This feature-length sequel to the acclaimed French comedy series Call My Agent! —a fun, four-season watch about a fictitious French talent agency that often featured real-life stars as clients—returns the original cast and features appearances by George Clooney, Jean Reno, Charlotte Gainsbourg, Beatrice Dalle, Monica Bellucci, all playing exaggerated versions of themselves. Set five years after the series finale, the story finds one-time talent agent Andrea (Camille Cottin) pursuing her dream to become a film director, only for her debut production to begin falling apart just days before filming.

Advertisement

Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!

5 / 21

77
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Daniel Satinoff / Courtesy of Sundance Institute / Sony Pictures Classics

Rom-Com - dir. Josef Kubota Wladyka
In theaters September 25

Director Josef Kubota Wladyka (Manos Sucias, Catch the Fair One), working from a script written with Nicholas Huynh, dedicates this look at the life of a competitive ballroom dancer to his mother. After tragedy strikes in her life, Haru (Rinko Kikuchi) reluctantly returns to the dance studio and finds a connection with the new instructor, Fedir (Alberto Guerra). Dealing with grief in a tonally surprising way, Wladyka took home the Directing Award at this year's Sundance Film Festival.

Advertisement

Heart of the Beast

6 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Paramount

Action-Adventure/Thriller - dir. David Ayer
In theaters September 25

Director  David Ayer reunites with Brad Pitt, the star of his 2014 film Fury, for this survival thriller written by Cameron Alexander. Pitt plays James Belmont, a Special Forces veteran who, along with his combat dog Odin, is stranded in the Alaskan wilderness after their plane crashes. After two Jason Statham-starring action pics (The Beekeeper and A Working Man), Ayer will take on a man vs. nature story like Joe Carnahan did in The Grey.

Advertisement

The History of Concrete

7 / 21

81
MetascoreUniversal acclaim
Photo by John Wilson / Courtesy of Sundance Institute / Magnolia

Documentary - dir. John Wilson
In theaters September 18

Fans of How to With John Wilson should happily embrace this feature-length documentary full of Wilson's surprising diversions fueled by his witty curiosity in the mundane. Attendance at a class on how to write Hallmark movies, a trip to Rome to see ancient concrete structures, and then a detour to the oldest concrete road in America are just a few of the tangents that come together to form Wilson's idiosyncratic and hilarious look at humanity.

Advertisement

Hope

8 / 21

68
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Plus M Entertainment / Neon

Foreign/Action/Drama/Horror/Sci-Fi/Thriller - dir. Na Hong-jin
In theaters September 9

For fans of The Wailing (a Metacritic Must-See), it has been a long ten-year wait for a new film from writer-director Na Hong-jin (The Yellow Sea, The Chaser). Set in the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, this action-packed entertainment follows a police chief (Hwang Jung- min), his officer (Hoyeon), and a band of locals as they face off against mysterious creatures played by Michael Fassbender, Alicia Vikander, Taylor Russell, and Cameron Britton. When Hope debuted at Cannes this year, most critics were impressed by the filmmaking in the first hour, but some were less satisfied as the film continued for another hour and a half.

Advertisement

Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie

9 / 21

83
MetascoreUniversal acclaim
Photo by Rachel Eliza Griffiths / Courtesy of Sundance Institute / Abramorama

Documentary - dir. Alex Gibney
In theaters September 17

Using narration from Salman Rushdie's 2024 memoir Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder and footage shot by his wife, Rachel Eliza Griffiths, Alex Gibney tells the story of the day Rushdie was attacked at the Chautauqua Institute, his difficult recovery, and his eventual return to public life. But the director also explores Rushdie's life as an artist living under threat for decades, since Iran's leader Ayatollah Khomeini issued a fatwa calling for the author's death after the publication of The Satanic Verses. For Vulture critic Bilge Ebiri, it's an "informative, moving, and, yes, occasionally infuriating work."

Advertisement

Mayday

10 / 21

60
MetascoreMixed or average
Photo by Apple

Action-Adventure/Comedy - dir. John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein
Streams on Apple TV beginning September 4

The latest action-comedy from the Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves writer-director duo of Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley is a Cold War spy thriller riff that finds Ryan Reynolds playing a U.S. Navy pilot stranded behind enemy lines while on a top-secret mission in the U.S.S.R. But he forms an unlikely bond with the ex-KGB agent who discovers him (Kenneth Branagh).

Advertisement

Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger

11 / 21

78
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Walt Disney Studios/Courtesy of La Biennale di Venezia

Documentary/Music - dir. Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern
In theaters (and IMAX) September 11

Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern, the directors of 2000s New York indie music scene chronicle Meet Me in the Bathroom, are at the helm of this documentary that chronicles the reunion of Liam and Noel Gallagher and the record-breaking tour, Oasis Live '25, that followed. Featuring the first joint interview with Noel and Liam in over 20 years, as well as rehearsal, backstage, and live concert footage, it's an uplifting look at what the music of Oasis means to their fans all around the world. The film is also expected to stream on Disney+ and Hulu later this year.

Advertisement

Onslaught

12 / 21

57
MetascoreMixed or average
Photo by A24

Action/Horror/Thriller - dir. Adam Wingard
In theaters (and IMAX) September 4

After Godzilla vs. Kong and Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire, director Adam Wingard returns to the town of Moriarty, New Mexico and the world of The Guest with co-writer Simon Barrett for this action-packed genre flick about rogue super soldiers who meet their match in the RV park where Celeste (Adria Arjona), a PTSD-suffering veteran, lives with her young daughter (Blake Kennedy). She gets a little help from a fellow vet played by Die Hard's Reginald VelJohnson as she faces off against the creations of Hans and Hanna Kammler (Dan Stevens and Rebecca Hall).

Advertisement

Practical Magic 2

13 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Warner Bros. Pictures

Fantasy/Comedy - dir. Susanne Bier
In theaters September 11

It has been almost 30 years since Practical Magic, starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman as witches Sally and Gillian Owens, hit theaters, but they are back this month with Aunt Frances (Stockard Channing), Aunt Jet (Dianne Wiest) and, unfortunately the same curse for a new generation (Joey King, Maisie Williams)—those they fall in love with will suffer an untimely death. Based on The Book of Magic, Alice Hoffman 's follow-up to her original novel, and directed by Susanne Bier, who has struggled to find favor with critics since her 2010 feature In a Better World, this long-awaited sequel also stars Lee Pace and Xolo Maridueña.

Advertisement

Primetime

14 / 21

74
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by A24

Action/Drama/Thriller - dir. Lance Oppenheim
In theaters September 25

Director Lance Oppenheim moves from documentary (Some Kind of Heaven, Spermworld) to narrative filmmaking with this look at TV's To Catch a Predator. Last year, that reality series was also the subject of David Osit's documentary Predators, a Metacritic Must-See. Oppenheim's film focuses on the show's host, Chris Hansen, played by Robert Pattinson, and his thirst to turn his show into a primetime success. The strong supporting cast includes Merritt Wever, Skyler Gisondo, Anna Faris, Phoebe Bridgers, and Bokeem Woodbine.

Advertisement

Resident Evil

15 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Sony/Columbia Pictures/Dušan Martinček

Horror - dir. Zach Cregger
In theaters (and IMAX) September 18

Following the success of Barbarian and Weapons, writer-director Zach Cregger jumps into the world of video game adaptation with his take on Capcom's Resident Evil franchise. Unlike Paul W. S. Anderson's more action-oriented take with Milla Jovovich, Cregger will lean into the horror aspects of the game as he follows Bryan (Austin Abrams), a medical courier trying to survive one chaotic night in Raccoon City. Paul Walter Hauser, Kali Reis, and Zach Cherry also star in what could end up being the best-reviewed video game adaptation of all time—admittedly, a low bar to clear.

Advertisement

The Scout

16 / 21

72
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Greenwich Entertainment

Drama/Comedy - dir. Paula González-Nasser
In theaters September 25 (more cities October 2)

Drawing from her own experience, writer-director Paula González-Nasser's debut feature captures a day in the life of Sophia (Mimi Davila), a young location scout for a TV production in New York City. As Sophia visits various neighborhoods, enters different shops and apartments, and interacts with the people working and living in those spaces, while also trying to meet the demands of her employers, González-Nasser explores the rewards and the costs of working as a young artist in the city.

Advertisement

Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom

17 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by GKIDS/Aardman Animations Ltd

Animation/Family - dir. Steve Cox and Matthew Walker
In theaters September 18

A new stop-motion feature from Aardman Animations is always something to celebrate, whether it's another adventure for Wallace and Gromit (Wallace & Gromit: Vengeance Most Fowl), the underrated one-offs The Pirates! Band of Misfits and Early Man, or, in this case, the third film starring Shaun the Sheep, following 2015's Shaun the Sheep Movie and 2010's A Shaun the Sheep Movie: Farmageddon. Set before Halloween, this fun family adventure follows Shaun as his attempt to revive the flock's pumpkin patch quickly spins out of control.

Advertisement

Unabomber

18 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Philippe Bosse/Netflix

Drama/Thriller - dir. Janus Metz
Streams on Netflix beginning September 25

Jacob Tremblay portrays Ted Kaczynski in this biographical thriller that flashes back and forth between two time periods: one tracing the domestic terrorist's consequential teenage years in the late 1950s and another during the FBI-led manhunt to catch him in the 1990s. Russell Crowe, Shailene Woodley, and Annabelle Wallis also star.

Advertisement

The Uprising

19 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Focus Features

Action/Drama - dir. Paul Greengrass
In theaters September 11

As he did with 2002's Bloody Sunday, 2006's United 93, and 2013's Captain Phillips, all Metacritic Must-Sees, writer-director Paul Greengrass once again tackles a historic event in his new film. But this time it's one that took place centuries ago—the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 (also known as Wat Tyler's Rebellion or The Great Uprising). Andrew Garfield stars as a grieving farmer whose rebellion against the oppressive taxes of the young King Richard II turns him into a leader of thousands. The impressive supporting cast includes Jamie Bell, Stephen Dillane, Katherine Waterston, Tom Hollander, Cosmo Jarvis, Thomasin McKenzie, and Woody Norman.

Advertisement

The Weight

20 / 21

70
MetascoreGenerally favorable
Photo by Matteo Cocco / Courtesy of Sundance Institute / Vertical

Action-Adventure - dir. Padraic McKinley
In theaters September 18

Padraic McKinley makes his feature directing debut with this story set in 1933 Oregon. Ethan Hawke plays Samuel Murphy, a battle-scarred veteran and widow sent to a work camp led by Warden Clancy (Russell Crowe). Observing Murphy's ingenuity, Clancy offers him a deal—help smuggle a fortune of gold through 100 miles of wilderness and he'll be released and able to reunite with his daughter. Reviews from the film's premiere at this year's Sundance Film Festival praise Hawke's performance in this tense journey of survival.

Advertisement

Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

21 / 21

tbd
Metascore
Photo by Amazon MGM Studios

Action/Drama/Thriller - dir. Bassam Tariq
In theaters September 25 (more cities in October)

At one time, writer-director Bassam Tariq (Mogul Mowgli, These Birds Walk) and star Mahershala Ali were attached to Marvel's Blade reboot. While that film never left development, this story of a devoutly religious Houston hitman who struggles to protect his children after this wife dies, could prove far more intriguing. The strong supporting cast includes John Cho, Tramell Tillman, Giancarlo Esposito, Tiffany Boone, Abubakr Ali, and Laith Nakli.

Privacy Policy

Manage Consent Preferences

Social Media Cookies

These cookies are set by a range of social media services that we have added to the site to enable you to share our content with your friends and networks. They are capable of tracking your browser across other sites and building up a profile of your interests. This may impact the content and messages you see on other websites you visit. If you do not allow these cookies you may not be able to use or see these sharing tools.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.
